notes: ACTIVE relation pack (upgraded from pilot). No invented Sn/Sp. Traditional MTrP maps labeled traditional. No Travell verbatim.

relations.source_structure: hip joint / periarticular hip (FAI-related, osteoarthritis, GTPS continuum)
relations.target_region: buttock / posterior pelvic / lateral lumbar-flank perceived pain
relations.clinical_context: Lumbopelvic pain with sitting, squatting, or hip rotation that does not follow a clear radicular pattern; lumbar tests poorly reproduce familiar pain.
supporting_evidence: Hip–spine syndrome recognized clinically; hip exam can alter perceived lumbar-buttock symptoms
FADIR/FABER interpreted by pain location; negative lumbar neural tests do not prove lumbar source

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: No single test cleanly separates hip vs lumbar; do not invent Sn/Sp.

limitations: Hip and lumbar often coexist
Imaging morphology of hip ≠ pain generator
recommended_examination: Hip ROM + FADIR/FABER with familiar-pain mapping
Lumbar AROM, SLR/crossed SLR, neurological screen
Ask which movement most reproducibly changes symptoms

references.citation: Reiman MP, et al. Concordance of hip and lumbar examination findings — clinical hip–spine literature and exam reviews.
Delitto A et al. Low Back Pain: Clinical Practice Guidelines (JOSPT) — screening and classification framing.

relations.source_structure: lumbar nerve root / sciatic pathway (clinical radiculopathy construct)
relations.clinical_context: Leg-dominant or mixed lumbopelvic-leg pain with neurological clues but SLR negative or non-familiar.
supporting_evidence: SLR diagnostic performance is variable across reviews and thresholds
Crossed SLR more specific but not a standalone exclusion tool when negative either

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Qualitative only: negative SLR does not exclude radiculopathy. Do not invent LR−.

limitations: Irritability, chronicity, and examiner technique alter results
Back-dominant pain may yield negative SLR despite lumbar contribution
alternative_explanations: Peripheral entrapment (less common — do not leap)
recommended_examination: Crossed SLR / slump as adjuncts with familiar symptoms

references.citation: van der Windt DA et al. Physical examination for lumbar radiculopathy due to disc herniation in patients with low-back pain (Cochrane Database) — qualitative limitations of single tests.
Delitto A et al. Low Back Pain CPG. JOSPT.

relations.source_structure: lumbar zygapophyseal / mechanical extension-rotation pain construct
relations.clinical_context: Mechanical LBP suspected; Kemp/extension-rotation negative or non-specific.
supporting_evidence: Facet clinical tests have limited structural validity
Single provocation maneuvers do not confirm or exclude facetogenic pain

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Do not treat Kemp as inclusion or exclusion criterion for 'facet syndrome'.

limitations: Construct of clinical facet pain is controversial
Positive Kemp is non-specific
recommended_examination: Pattern of aggravating movements and load tolerance

references.citation: Hancock MJ et al. Systematic review of tests to identify the disc, SIJ or facet joint as source of low back pain — limited utility of many clinical tests.
Qaseem A et al. Noninvasive treatments for acute, subacute, and chronic low back pain (ACP guideline) — avoid over-pathologizing.

relations.source_structure: lumbar somatic structures (disc / zygapophyseal / soft tissue — clinical referred pain)
relations.target_region: buttock / posterior or lateral thigh (non-dermatomal possible)
relations.clinical_context: Buttock or thigh pain without hard neurological signs; lumbar movements reproduce familiar pain better than local hip/knee tests.
supporting_evidence: Somatic referred pain from lumbar structures is a standard clinical construct in LBP CPGs
Absence of SLR does not refute somatic referral

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Referral maps are clinical patterns, not precise lesion localization.

limitations: Cannot name exact tissue from referral alone
Must screen hip and red flags
recommended_examination: Lumbar repeated movements / AROM with familiar pain

references.citation: Bogduk N. On the definitions and physiology of back pain, referred pain, and radicular pain (clinical framing).
Delitto A et al. Low Back Pain CPG. JOSPT.

relations.source_structure: cauda equina / severe lumbar canal compromise (emergency construct)
relations.clinical_context: New saddle anesthesia, bladder/bowel dysfunction, or progressive bilateral neurological deficit with LBP/leg symptoms.
supporting_evidence: Emergency referral pathways in LBP CPGs and national guidance

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Clinical red-flag pathway — not a special-test accuracy claim. Do not invent Sn/Sp for individual questions.

limitations: Individual red-flag questions have imperfect accuracy — act on constellation and urgency
recommended_examination: Urgent medical / ED referral per local pathway
Do not continue elective MSK hypothesis hunting

references.citation: NICE / national low back pain and sciatica guidance — cauda equina emergency symptoms (use local current pathway).
Delitto A et al. Low Back Pain CPG. JOSPT — red flag screening framing.

relations.clinical_context: Unilateral LBP or buttock pain changing with extension-rotation; non-dermatomal; after red-flag screen.
supporting_evidence: Experimental lumbar facet provocation maps show buttock/thigh referral patterns
Maps ≠ office test that names a facet level

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Provocation maps are not Sn/Sp of Kemp or palpation.

limitations: Segment overlap
Cannot diagnose facet level from a pain drawing

references.citation: McCall IW, Park WM, O'Brien JP. Induced pain referral from posterior lumbar elements. Spine.
Fukui S et al. Distribution of referred pain from the lumbar zygapophyseal joints and dorsal rami. Clin J Pain.

relations.target_region: buttock / posterior pelvic / low lumbar perceived
relations.clinical_context: Buttock-dominant pain; lumbar neural tests weak; possible pregnancy, trauma, or asymmetric load history.
supporting_evidence: SIJ clinical diagnosis remains limited; clusters of provocation tests preferred over single maneuvers
Hancock systematic review: limited utility of many SIJ tests

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Do not invent Sn/Sp for thigh thrust or FABER as SIJ confirmation.

limitations: Positive provocation non-specific
Often coexists with lumbar pain
recommended_examination: Multi-test SIJ provocation cluster only as limited screen
Do not label SIJ from one positive test

references.citation: Hancock MJ et al. Systematic review of tests to identify disc, SIJ or facet as source of LBP.
Laslett M. Evidence-based diagnosis and treatment of the painful sacroiliac joint — cluster framing (qualitative).

relations.clinical_context: Lumbopelvic pain with dual reproduction on lumbar and hip testing (hip–spine syndrome pattern).
supporting_evidence: Hip–spine coexistence is clinically recognized
Treating one region alone may fail when both contribute

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Coexistence is clinical reasoning, not a single accuracy metric.

limitations: Do not force a single-label diagnosis
Prioritize cauda / progressive neuro first
recommended_examination: Document which tests reproduce familiar pain in which region

references.citation: Reiman MP et al. Concordance of hip and lumbar examination findings — hip–spine literature.
Delitto A et al. Low Back Pain CPG. JOSPT.

relations.clinical_context: Leg-dominant pain ± neurological clues: use SLR/crossed SLR + neuro screen + history — not one test.
supporting_evidence: Cochrane and CPG framing: single neural tension tests imperfect; neurological exam essential
Familiar symptom reproduction required for meaning

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Cite cluster qualitatively; do not invent numeric LR for the battery in-app.

limitations: Irritability may limit testing
Does not replace imaging when management changes
recommended_examination: SLR and crossed SLR as tolerated

references.citation: van der Windt DA et al. Cochrane — physical examination for lumbar radiculopathy.
Delitto A et al. Low Back Pain CPG. JOSPT.

relations.target_region: bilateral or unilateral legs / buttock with walking
relations.clinical_context: Age-related walking-limited leg symptoms eased by flexion/sitting; differs from vascular claudication and from acute disc radiculopathy.
supporting_evidence: Clinical pattern of neurogenic claudication guides stenosis suspicion
Imaging findings common in asymptomatic older adults — do not over-attribute

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Pattern-based; no invented Sn/Sp for shopping-cart sign alone.

limitations: Vascular claudication overlap
MRI stenosis ≠ symptom generator
recommended_examination: Walking vs bicycle / flexion relief history

references.citation: Delitto A et al. Low Back Pain CPG — stenosis / classification framing. JOSPT.
NASS / lumbar stenosis clinical literature — neurogenic claudication pattern (qualitative).

relations.target_region: buttock / lateral hip / posterior thigh perceived
relations.clinical_context: Buttock pain with familiar pain on palpation after lumbar/hip/SIJ screens — traditional hypothesis only.
supporting_evidence: Traditional myofascial maps describe buttock/thigh patterns (traditional class only)
limitations: Must not replace cauda or radiculopathy reasoning
Traditional ≠ absolute anatomy
recommended_examination: Familiar-pain palpation as weak adjunct only

references.citation: Tough EA et al. 2007 — MTrP diagnostic criteria variability / caution.
Lucas N et al. Clin J Pain. 2009 — palpation reliability caution.

relations.source_structure: axial spondyloarthritis / inflammatory back pain construct
relations.clinical_context: Younger adult; morning stiffness >30–60 min; night pain; improvement with activity; alternating buttock pain; extra-articular clues.
supporting_evidence: Inflammatory back-pain criteria used as screening prompts toward rheumatology, not as physio diagnosis

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Qualitative screening features; do not invent Sn/Sp for morning stiffness alone.

limitations: Mechanical LBP can have morning stiffness
Do not delay referral when constellation present
recommended_examination: Refer per local rheumatology pathway when indicated
Continue MSK care only as adjunct

references.citation: ASAS inflammatory back pain criteria / axial SpA referral framing (qualitative).
Delitto A et al. Low Back Pain CPG — medical screening framing. JOSPT.
